title: When Is Kramers-Wannier Duality Invertible?
authors: Akash Sinha, Pramod Padmanabhan, Vladimir Korepin
abstract: {\it Kramers-Wannier} duality of the quantum Ising chain is naturally realized as a noninvertible transformation on a finite periodic chain. Upon incorporating appropriate symmetry-twisted sectors, however, the duality can be promoted to an invertible unitary transformation. In this Letter, we classify when the Kramers-Wannier duality admits an invertible realization on a finite Hilbert space. We show that this is determined by the representation of the Ising bond algebra and establish a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of its two central elements. This representation-theoretic criterion unifies the conventional noninvertible realization with invertible constructions involving symmetry-twisted sectors and applies equally to other models with the same underlying bond algebra. As an explicit example, we find an order-disorder duality in a non-trivial realization of the Ising bond algebra that admits an invertible Kramers-Wannier duality.
summary: This work provides a deep, representation-theoretic criterion to determine when the Kramers-Wannier duality for the quantum Ising chain is invertible on a finite lattice. By analyzing the bond algebra's central elements, the authors establish that the condition $	ext{Tr } P_o = 	ext{Tr } P_e$ is necessary and sufficient for this duality to be realized as a unitary transformation.
main_problem: The paper aims to classify the necessary and sufficient conditions under which the Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality, naturally noninvertible for finite periodic chains, can be promoted to an invertible unitary transformation.
main_result: Invertibility of the KW duality is determined by a representation-theoretic criterion: the trace of two central elements of the underlying bond algebra must be equal ($	ext{Tr } P_o = 	ext{Tr } P_e$).
method: The analysis employs representation theory applied to the bond algebra generated by local terms of the quantum Ising chain, decomposing the Hilbert space into sectors defined by central elements.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the quantum Ising chain, whose dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian constructed from local terms forming a bond algebra. The duality relates strong-coupling and weak-coupling regimes.
key_observables: The traces of the central elements $P_o$ and $P_e$, and the existence of symmetry-twisted sectors.
important_parameters: The coupling constant $g$, which governs the duality transformation between $g$ and $1/g$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of representation theory to the bond algebra and relies on constructing specific symmetry operators ($\eta_-$) to define the unitary duality.
figures_summary: The notes reference a TABLE I summarizing the representation-theoretic hierarchy of finite-size KW duality based on trace conditions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem, uses the bond algebra and central elements ($P_o, P_e$) to formulate the condition $	ext{Tr } P_o = 	ext{Tr } P_e$, and then proves this condition is necessary and sufficient for constructing the invertible unitary duality operator $D$.
why_interesting: The rigorous classification of when a fundamental duality symmetry becomes unitary is crucial for understanding the exact solvability and symmetries of quantum many-body systems, connecting algebraic structure to physical realizability.
